10.1002_adfm.79326: Thermal safety is a key challenge for high‐energy lithium metal batteries. Conventional separators deform under overheating while sustaining ion transport, accelerating thermal runaway. Herein, we report an aramid‐supported shape memory separator that converts temperature rise into reconstruction of ion transport pathways. A covalently crosslinked PETMP‐TMPTA‐IBOA network is photopolymerized within a porous aramid scaffold. At normal operating temperatures, the interconnected pore structure affords an ionic conductivity of 0.29 mS cm −1 and enables stable Li plating/stripping for over 3000 h. At 140°C, the shape memory network undergoes thermomechanical rearrangement, constricting the percolating pores and increasing the ionic resistance by one order of magnitude. Meanwhile, the aramid scaffold preserves dimensional integrity up to 175°C and maintains electrode isolation after ionic shutdown. The separator is compatible with high‐energy NCM811 and Li‐rich Mn‐based oxide cathodes. In particular, a Li‐rich cathode with high mass loading of 16 mg cm −2 cycles stably for 100 cycles at 0.5 C, delivers nearly 250 mAh g −1 at 60°C, and remains operable up to 125°C. This work establishes thermomechanical reconstruction of ion transport pathways as a general design principle for intrinsically self‐protective lithium metal batteries that reconcile high energy operation with autonomous overheating protection.
10.1016_j.est.2026.122960: This study employs classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, utilizing an amorphization and recrystallization (A + R) modelling framework, to comprehensively investigate the structural, thermodynamic, and ion transport behaviours of TiO₂ nanospheres intercalated with lithium (Li + ), sodium (Na + ), and magnesium (Mg 2+ ) ions. Atomistic models of mixed-phase TiO₂ nanospheres (15,972 atoms) were constructed, thermally amorphized at 7000 K, and then randomly intercalated with Li + , Na + , and Mg 2+ at molar fractions (x) of 0.11, 0.15, 0.19, and 0.23. These systems underwent controlled annealing and gradual cooling from 1500 K to 0 K to induce recrystallization and stabilization, mimicking synthesis and cycling conditions relevant to high-performance Li-, Na-, and Mg-ion batteries. Interatomic forces were described by the Born model with long-range Coulombic and short-range Buckingham potentials, incorporating a core-shell model for oxygen polarizability. The simulations revealed that both the type and concentration of intercalated ions critically influenced the structural stability and ionic transport efficiency of the TiO₂ nanospheres. Mg 2+ ions exhibited superior retention within the TiO₂ matrix compared to Li + and Na + , indicating strong thermodynamic stability and preference for embedded positions. Conversely, higher concentrations of Li + ions displayed enhanced surface migration due to their smaller radius and weaker electrostatic interactions, while Na + ions showed intermediate diffusional behaviours. Li + consistently demonstrated the highest diffusivity across all concentrations and temperatures, attributed to its smaller ionic radius (0.76 Å) and monovalent nature, resulting in weaker electrostatic interactions with the host lattice. Despite theoretical predictions of higher diffusion barriers for Mg 2+ , simulated activation energies were remarkably low (0.08–0.21 eV for Mg 2+ , 0.19–0.25 eV for Na + , and 0.18–0.37 eV for Li + ), suggesting kinetic advantages in an idealized, defect-controlled environment. Further analysis through slow cooling protocols showed that while Li + and Na + ions initially expelled at high temperatures re-diffused into the Ti O framework or near-surface sites below 1000 K, Mg 2+ ions remained stably intercalated throughout the cooling process, highlighting their excellent thermal stability. Microstructural evaluations confirmed the formation of well-ordered crystalline domains, predominantly brookite and rutile polymorphs, interspersed with functional tunnel-like defects and vacancies, which enhance ion mobility and structural robustness. MgₓTiO₂ systems, particularly at high concentrations (x = 0.23), exhibited the most thermodynamically stable structures, forming distinct multiphase crystalline architectures favourable for mechanical and thermal resilience. These findings underscore the potential of LiₓTiO₂, NaₓTiO₂, and MgₓTiO₂ nanospheres as promising anode materials for next-generation metal-ion batteries, offering a balanced combination of structural robustness, efficient ion transport, and thermal resilience for high-power and long-life energy storage applications.
10.1021_jacs.6c00770: Water electrolysis for concurrent green chemical synthesis and hydrogen production represents a pivotal strategy to address global energy challenges. Ethylene glycol (EG) serves as a promising alternative anodic reactant to the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to its lower oxidation potential. However, industrial application of Pd-based catalysts remains limited by their tendency for oxidative deactivation. Herein, we fabricate a PdAu2/Ni1–xO catalyst for EG oxidation reaction (EGOR), which exhibits exceptional activity with potentials of 0.99 and 1.09 V vs RHE at 1.0 and 2.0 A cm–2, respectively. Integrated experimental and computational studies reveal that Ni1–xO supplies *OH species, while Au and Pd lower the energy barriers for O–H and C–H cleavage, respectively. Such synergistic mechanism facilitates the continuous reaction of EG and prevented the oxidative deactivation of Pd. In an integrated EGOR∥HER system, stable operation at 500 mA cm–2 was sustained for 320 h at voltages well below conventional water electrolysis, with successful scaling to kW-level (6 cells, 100 A@10.2 V). This work establishes an energy-efficient, dual-product electrochemical manufacturing paradigm through effective anode–cathode coupling.
10.1038_s41467-025-66545-7: Membranes selective to ions of the same charge are increasingly sought for water waste processing and valuable element recovery. However, while narrow channels are known to be essential, other membrane parameters remain difficult to identify and control. Here we show that Zr⁴⁺, Sn⁴⁺, Ir⁴⁺, and La³⁺ ions intercalated into vermiculite laminate membranes become effectively unexchangeable, creating stable channels, one to two water layers wide, that exhibit robust and tuneable ion selectivity. Ion permeability in these membranes spans five orders of magnitude, following a trend dictated by the ions' Gibbs free energy of hydration. Unexpectedly, different intercalated ions lead to two distinct monovalent ion selectivity sequences, despite producing channels of identical width. The selectivity instead correlates with the membranes' stiffness and the entropy of hydration of the intercalated ions. These results introduce an ion selectivity mechanism driven by entropic and mechanical effects, beyond classical size and charge exclusion.
10.1039_d6ta04725d: A P2-type layered oxide delivers exceptional long-term sodium-storage performance through highly reversible Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ redox chemistry, achieving 93.04% capacity retention after 80 000 cycles over a wide temperature range.
10.26599_nr.2026.94908452: The design of metal-free electrocatalysts for efficient biomass-based cinnamaldehyde (CAL) conversion to high-value-added 3-phenylpropanol (HCOL) and the insight into their catalytic mechanism have drawn considerable attention. However, they remained challenging due to the unclear complicated hydrogenation pathways. Here, metal-free mesoporous polymer-based electrocatalysts were synthesized, for the first time, for the electrochemical hydrogenation of CAL to HCOL. The catalysts consist of phytic acid (PA)-doped mesoporous poly(m-phenylenediamine) (coined meso-PA/PmPD) with high specific surface areas up to 95.3 m2/g. The optimized meso-PA/PmPD exhibits a record-high performance with high Faradaic efficiency (93.5%) and selectivity (97.5%), far surpassing all the reported electrocatalysts (Faradaic efficiency < 55% and selectivity < 25%). Mechanistic studies reveal that meso-PA/PmPD induces the parallel-configuration adsorption of CAL via π–π and hydrogen-bonding interactions, reducing the energy barriers for CAL carbonyl hydrogenation with active hydrogen (H*) to COL and its subsequent hydrogenation to HCOL, thereby boosting the HCOL selectivity. Meanwhile, an appropriate PA doping amount accelerates water dissociation to generate H* and interfacial charge transfer. The mesoporous structure facilitates CAL mass transport into the catalyst interior to promote its conversion. This study provides novel insight into the electroreduction mechanism of CAL, guiding the design of high-performance biomass-conversion electrocatalysts through rationally structural engineering of porous polymers.
10.34133_research.0788: Water electrolysis is a key industrial process for producing green hydrogen. To avoid the use of noble metals and fluorinated polymer membranes, liquid water electrolysis is often carried out in alkaline conditions. It is common to distinguish between 3 processes: alkaline electrolysis at high electrolyte concentrations (≥7 M) with porous membranes, alkaline electrolysis at high electrolyte concentrations (≥7 M) with ion-solvating membranes, and alkaline electrolysis at moderate electrolyte concentrations (<2 M) with anion-exchange membranes. Here, we consider the fundamental aspects of water and ion fluxes and of conductivity across the 3 types of membranes. We discuss ionic currents governed by ion–ion interactions and those resulting from a Grotthuss mechanism. Furthermore, in the case of porous membranes made of a polymeric fabric with compressed inorganic fillers such as zirconia, which are negatively charged in the presence of KOH, and of ion-solvating membranes such as polybenzimidazole, which also become negatively charged by deprotonation at high pH, those membranes should be a weak cation exchanger. We here address this dichotomy. All in all, we show that in all 3 cases, the membrane is an anion exchanger where hydroxide ion mobility differs from that of adjacent aqueous solution due to confinement favoring a Grotthuss-type transport and a jump mechanism.
